title: Nuncio Filippo Acciaiuoli (Lisbon) to the Secretariat of State, 1758-60 (AAV Segr. Stato Portogallo 117, DECODE R25, R195-R201)

documents.shelfmark: AAV Segreteria di Stato, Portogallo 117, items 117/1-8 (DECODE R25, R195-R201)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment written above the cipher on R197, R198, R199; none on R25, R195, R196, R200, R201.

transcription.notes: Per record: R25 1918, R195 860, R196 492, R197 190, R198 577, R199 791, R200 1999, R201 1499 digits. Crossed-out groups not transcribed; scattered slips give unassigned pairs.

system.summary: Fixed-length 2-digit homophones for letters and common syllables/words, digit 6 a null, 4-digit nomenclator codes all beginning with 2 (Lasry reconstruction, DECODE 2020).
system.notes: No 2-digit element begins with 2 or contains 6, so parsing is deterministic.

prior_solution.where: Lasry's reconstructed key and letter-level decryption attached to the DECODE records (Oct 2020); codes unresolved, no Italian text; three leaves deciphered at the time

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE records R25, R195-R201 fetched with the session cookie: images, digit transcriptions, Lasry's key and decryption.
Lasry's reconstructed key and letter-level decryption of all eight records found attached to every record.
Decryption flattened per letter and split into Italian words by the model.
Contemporary decipherments on R197-R199 aligned with the cipher: 25 nomenclator codes fixed (Re, Regina, Spagna, tutto, molto, ministri ...).
Further codes from context (2740 prim-, 2530 chirurgo, 2394 conte, 2743 principessa).
Web search for an edition of Acciaiuoli's 1758 cipher despatches: none found.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per letter, the NiLan/Midas digit transcriptions (decode/DOC_*_D1656-1663), George Lasry's letter-level decryption of all eight (decode/DOC_R25_D3231_3231.txt) and this project's word-split reading copied from READING.md into texts/; key = Lasry's DOC_R25_D3232 plus the code table copied to texts/key.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): the eight texts/R*_decryption.md read through. R197-R199 (deciphered on the leaf) and R196 build sentences; R25, R195, R200 and R201 have an open <nnnn> code or gap in almost every sentence (13-38% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py). Those four relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read measured 0.246 (2,050 of 8,326 tokens).

DECODE record pages of R25, R195, R200, R201 re-fetched with the project cookie; their DOC_*.png attachments (described in NOTES as 'key and work images', never opened) downloaded: they are the Secretariat of State's clear decipherments and working drafts of R25 (ff. 90-93), R195 (ff. 94-95), R196, R198, R200 (ff. 107-113, two fair copies and a draft), R201 (ff. 161-162).
The clear decipherments of R25, R195, R200, R201 transcribed line by line from the images (texts/R*_decipherment.txt).

Each decipherment aligned word by word with the key decode (b12_dec.py, b12_align.py; texts/R*_align.tsv): ~65% of clear words carried letter by letter, ~25% by code groups whose implied values agree across the four letters (2300 tutt-, 2171 molt-, 2189 quest-, 2530 Marchese, 2774 Re, 2803 Segretario, 2823 Sua Maestà ...); the rest fall where DECODE's digit transcription is garbled. Key correction: 03 = per, not nel. READING.md's 2530 = chirurgo withdrawn.

R195 line 11 re-read on the cipher image where the decipherer left a hole ('non s'intende'): 2180 14 55 75 05 59 98 55 98 53 = 'poiché non ha da durari' (DECODE: '2 1 8 0 ? 4 5 5 ...'); the draft agrees. R195 line 3 ('pare solamente assicurato') checked on the image and not explained by the key.
_check_reading.py on the reading bodies: R25 0.87, R195 0.91, R200 1.0, R201 0.95 clean sentences. All eight letters now read; fraction_read 1.0.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): R25 and R195 readings had no '## Reading' heading, so the sweep scored header and notes; heading added, bodies re-scored: R25 plain 0.526 -> 0.87, R195 0.448 -> 0.818 (explicit 1.0, 0.818); both keep read. R196 had no reading file (the sweep scored Lasry's raw decode, plain 0.355): its clear decipherment DOC_R196_D1449 (f. 97r) transcribed and compared with the decode, reading texts/R196_reading.md and _en.md written, plain 1.0 (7/7); keeps read, grade A.

texts.label: 117/1 = R25, ff. 95r-95v, 12 Sept 1758
texts.summary: The nuncio's secret account of the attempt of 3 Sept 1758 on José I: coming back from a lady "delle prime famiglie" (the young Marchioness of Távora), the king was fired on in his calesse, his valet and favourite Pedro Teixeira badly wounded and the king hit in the right arm. The blow was thought to come from her relatives or from Teixeira's enemies.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1757, Italian, modern spelling: the plain share is the bar): the sweep scored the whole file, header and notes included (plain 0.526, explicit 0.737). '## Reading' heading added before the body; body alone: plain 0.87 (20/23), explicit 1.0 (23/23). The three failing sentences hold; their unknown words are the name Texeira, the marked [?Vilasso], and caualcante/bilancino/lasciandoui (period words the list lacks). Keeps read. Earlier: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R25_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R25_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 0.87 (20 of 23 sentences); 'Vilasso' after Texeira kept from the decipherment, unconfirmed by the figures.

texts.label: 117/2 = R195, f. 98r, Sept 1758
texts.summary: The public version of the king's injury is illness; the arm is said to be broken. Fleets and ships are held back, to the merchants' loss.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1757, Italian, plain share is the bar): the sweep scored the whole file with notes (plain 0.448, explicit 0.655). '## Reading' heading added; body alone: plain 0.818 (9/11), explicit 0.818 (9/11). The two failing sentences are the two [?] stretches the figures do not confirm ('pare [?solamente] [?assicurato]' and one in the last paragraph); the rest holds. Keeps read. Earlier: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R195_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R195_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 0.91 (10 of 11 sentences); the decipherer's one hole ('poiché non . . .', margin 'non s'intende') read on the cipher image: 'poiché non ha da durare', as in the draft; two stretches not confirmed by the transcribed figures are marked [?].

texts.label: 117/3 = R196, f. 101r, 26 Sept 1758
texts.summary: The public version is illness: the arm is said to stay impeded and the king is in bed all day.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1758, Italian, plain share is the bar): the entry named no reading and the sweep scored Lasry's raw decryption (decode/DOC_R25_D3231_3231.txt, plain 0.355, explicit 0.774). The Secretariat's clear decipherment of R196 (f. 97r, 'Decif.ta li 28. Ott.', DECODE attachment DOC_R196_D1449; draft D1450 f. 98r) was transcribed (texts/R196_decipherment.txt) and compared clause by clause with the decode: all of it is in the figures (2754 pubblic-, 2131 ancora, 2823 Sua Maestà, 2141 come, 2349 avvis-, 2907 due, 2189 quest-, 2530 Marchesa, 03 per). Reading texts/R196_reading.md: plain 1.0 (7/7), explicit 1.0 (7/7). Earlier: Short letter; sentences build with a few open codes (6 of 9 clean): the rumours about the king's wound, the arm that will stay impaired.

texts.label: 117/4 = R197, f. 103r, 10 Oct 1758 (deciphered on the leaf)
texts.summary: Deciphered at the time on the leaf: the king is up but never out all day; most think the arm is badly damaged and will stay impaired.

reading_review.note: Deciphered on the leaf: the Secretariat's clear decipherment above the figures reads as Italian sentences, and the word-split key reading agrees with it.

texts.label: 117/5 = R198, f. 104r, 31 Oct 1758 (deciphered on the leaf)
texts.summary: Deciphered at the time on the leaf: abscess and fever, not erysipelas; the arm will stay impaired.

reading_review.note: Deciphered on the leaf: the Secretariat's clear decipherment above the figures reads as Italian sentences, and the word-split key reading agrees with it.

texts.label: 117/6 = R199, f. 106r, 24 Oct 1758 (deciphered on the leaf)
texts.summary: Deciphered at the time on the leaf: after the death of his sister, Queen Barbara of Spain, José says Ferdinand VI has promised to marry his daughter Maria Francisca, which the Spanish minister contradicts.

reading_review.note: Deciphered on the leaf: the Secretariat's clear decipherment above the figures reads as Italian sentences, and the word-split key reading agrees with it.

texts.label: 117/7 = R200, ff. 115r-115v, 28 [Nov?] 1758
texts.summary: Carvalho (Pombal) is despotic and the king fears him; the court, the Infantes and the confessors; the expulsion of Jesuits and a lay brother of the Society; the nuncio is distrusted.

reading_review.note: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R200_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R200_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 1.0 (31 of 31 sentences); checked against the second fair copy and the draft; 2803 = Segretario (draft); the ambassador code 2339 left blank by the decipherer read 'Ambasciatore di [?Spagna]' from the draft.

texts.label: 117/8 = R201, f. 280r, Lisbon 12 [?] 1760
texts.summary: Conferences of the Conde d'Oeiras (Carvalho); the Princess of Brazil's marriage to Infante Don Luis of Spain or to Don Pedro; London is alarmed at a Bourbon on the Portuguese throne. The marriage to Don Pedro took place in June 1760.

reading_review.note: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R201_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R201_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 0.95 (18 of 19 sentences); a second clear text of the letter is f. 162 (D1416).
